title: Eventual vanishing on punctured neighborhoods
statement: Let T be a spectral space, Z a closed subset with compact open complement, A an abelian sheaf on T, and q a natural number. Let D be the punctured-neighborhood cohomology diagram and C its canonical restriction cocone [def-weil-pbc-punctured-neighborhood-cohomology-diagram]. If x in D_N maps to zero under C_N, there is a compact open neighborhood M contained in N such that the restriction D(N→M)(x) is zero.

proof.text: Construct the explicit reverse-inclusion system, prove directedness and spectrality of stages and transition inclusions, and identify its topological limit with the punctured generalizations.
Use the proved puncturedGeneralizations_spectral theorem of the concrete spectral-system module to provide the spectral-space instance on the punctured generalizations.

Use the restriction coefficient presentation and its cohomology comparison isomorphisms. The normalized pullback families are the canonical ones; their IsPullback proofs are the choose_spec of the existing existence theorem.
Transport the class by eH and its zero-image equation by eL. Apply the general spectral-limit eventual-zero theorem to obtain a later index and a zero transition class.

The coefficient-presentation transition equation identifies the resulting zero class with eH applied to the ordinary restriction. Cancel the injective isomorphism eH and use the reverse-inclusion inequality to construct the required opposite-category arrow.

lean.statement: theorem puncturedNeighborhood_cohomology_eventual_zero {T : Type u} [TopologicalSpace T] [SpectralSpace T] (Z : Set T) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hU : IsCompact Zᶜ) (A : CategoryTheory.Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology T) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (q : ℕ) (N : (compactOpenNeighborhoods Z)ᵒᵖ) (x : (puncturedNeighborhoodCohomologyDiagram Z hZ A q).obj N) (hx : ((puncturedNeighborhoodCohomologyCocone Z hZ A q).ι.app N).hom x = 0) : ∃ (M : (compactOpenNeighborhoods Z)ᵒᵖ) (f : N ⟶ M), ((puncturedNeighborhoodCohomologyDiagram Z hZ A q).map f).hom x = 0
